name: Olivia Nielsen
episode: The worker who couldn't read the joke
life: “I still remember softening a translated word that later caused an argument.” Tuesday often includes a stop at the public end of the South Shore boardwalk, where Olivia checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I translated it too gently the first time. My friend deserves to know which actual word upset everybody.
appearance: Olivia has a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears, a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth, and a favorite piece of clothing, a mustard canvas overshirt. It usually goes with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. When somebody else has the floor, Olivia folds a paper napkin into quarters without noticing.
personality: Likes beautiful, unnecessary things and gets cross with people who mistake poverty for a lack of taste. Olivia takes longer choosing a cheap birthday card than an expensive coat.
agenda: To translate the hurtful word accurately.
family: Harold Pike is Olivia’s older cousin. Olivia chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Harold brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The tide clock*, Harold says, “I used to tell time from harbor smells. I took the new hire along on my early round.”
connections: Darcy Fadel (dock colleague). A truthful translation gives the photographed worker the words to challenge the apparent laugh.

reactions.situation: A relative forwards the break-room picture
reactions.response: Olivia asks that the picture stop traveling while the worker decides what to say.

reactions.situation: A witness is embarrassed about remembering only a little
reactions.response: Olivia asks where they stood and what they could hear, leaving the rest open instead of filling it with guesses.

reactions.situation: When a relative dismisses a little luxury
reactions.response: Olivia asks which ordinary pleasure the relative would give up first.
